Two ways to buy:  - `buy`: buyer `usdt.approve(this, amount)` then calls `buy` - one contract, two signatures    the first time, one signature (`buy`) on every purchase after a max approval.  - `settlePurchase`: buyer just `usdt.transfer(this, amount)` directly - a single signature,    every time, no approval ever - but someone has to notice the transfer and call    `settlePurchase` on the buyer's behalf, since plain ERC20 `transfer` has no callback hook.    That's `relayer`'s job (see the off-chain watcher in client/relayXonVendingMachine.js). `settlePurchase` trusts `relayer` to report the right buyer/amount/txHash, but never trusts it with the contract's actual funds: it only ever pays out XON backed by USDT that has genuinely, verifiably landed in this contract's own balance (`accountedUsdt` tracks how much of the current USDT balance is already spoken for by a completed purchase, across both paths). A compromised relayer key can misattribute a real deposit to the wrong buyer; it can never manufacture a payout with no matching deposit. A third path, `settleExternalPurchase`, pays out XON for USDT paid on a *different* chain (AssetHub, or Ethereum via the sibling `EthUsdtGateway` contract) - see the standalone relayer service that watches all three sources. This one is honestly NOT backed by the same on-chain guarantee as `settlePurchase`: the USDT never touches this contract's own balance (it sits in an AssetHub collector account, or in `EthUsdtGateway` on Ethereum), so there is no local balance to verify against. `relayer` is fully trusted for this path - a compromised relayer key here really can manufacture payouts, unlike the native-USDT paths above. What bounds that is the owner-set external limits: `maxExternalPerDeposit` per payout, and `maxExternalPerDay` - an allowance that refills continuously at that much per 24 hours, so a stolen relayer key can take at most about one day's allowance before the owner notices and pauses. Both start at zero, so the external path pays nothing until the owner opts in with `setExternalLimits`. Keep the relayer key and the custody it implies (the AssetHub/Ethereum gateways' owner keys) secured accordingly. `settleExternalSwap` is the market-price version of `settleExternalPurchase`: instead of paying XON from the reserve at `rate`, it spends the same amount of USDT from this contract's own USDT inventory on Xode, swaps it for XON through Xode's DEX pool (via the XCM precompile and the runtime's XCM `AssetExchanger`), and pays the buyer whatever the swap returned, provided it is at least the buyer's `minXonOut`. It's bounded by the same external limits and trusts the relayer the same way, but there's no XON reserve to drain at a stale rate, and the price is the pool's. It only ever spends `accountedUsdt` - USDT already paid for by completed purchases or added with `fundUsdtInventory` - never a native deposit that hasn't been settled yet. The fixed `rate` can drift from the DEX price, and anyone can then buy here and sell there. Two things bound that: the Xode-native paths (`buy`, `settlePurchase`) have their own per-purchase limit and refilling daily allowance (`setNativeLimits`, starting at zero like the external ones), and an optional `rateKeeper` - a key that isn't the owner - may move `rate` toward the market by at most `maxRateStepBps` per `minRateUpdateInterval` (`updateRate`). `rate` is XON paid out per 1 whole USDT, expressed the way Solidity sees native value on Xode: `pallet_revive`'s `NativeToEthRatio` (1e18/1e12 = 1_000_000) rescales the chain's 12-decimal native `Balance` up to standard 18-decimal EVM/\"ether\" units at the call boundary, so `msg.value`/`.balance`/`.call{value:}` all use 18 decimals here regardless of the chain's underlying native decimals. USDT (a 6-decimal pallet-assets token) is unaffected by that ratio - its precompile reports raw pallet-assets balances. buy(uint256).notice: Buys XON with `usdtAmount` USDT at the current `rate`. Requires a prior `usdt.approve(address(this), usdtAmount)` from the caller.

cancelTreasuryChange().notice: The owner withdrawing its own proposal, or the guardian stopping one it didn't expect.

constructor.notice: `treasury_` is the only place the owner can withdraw XON / USDT to (a cold multisig in production) and `guardian_` the key or multisig that can pause and veto treasury changes - see `Custodial`. Both may start as `owner_` in development.

externalAvailable().notice: USDT that `settleExternalPurchase` can still pay for right now: the allowance left after recent payouts, refilled at `maxExternalPerDay` per 24 hours, never above `maxExternalPerDay`.

fundUsdtInventory(uint256).notice: Adds USDT to the inventory `settleExternalSwap` spends from (needs a prior `usdt.approve(address(this), amount)`). A plain transfer would look like a native purchase waiting to be settled, so inventory goes through here and is counted in `accountedUsdt`.

guardianPause().notice: The guardian can stop the contract (not restart it - that's the owner's `setPaused(false)`).

maxExternalPerDeposit().notice: Limits on `settleExternalPurchase`, in raw USDT units - see the contract docs.

maxNativePerPurchase().notice: Limits on the Xode-native paths (`buy`, `settlePurchase`), in raw USDT units, working like the external ones. They bound what arbitrage against the fixed `rate` can take when the DEX price moves away from it. Both start at zero: native purchases are off until the owner sets them.

nativeAvailable().notice: USDT that `buy` / `settlePurchase` can still take right now, refilled the same way.

pendingOwner().notice: Nominated by `transferOwnership`; becomes owner once it calls `acceptOwnership`.

quote(uint256).notice: Amount of XON `usdtAmount` USDT would currently buy, at zero cost/side effects.

rateKeeper().notice: May nudge `rate` toward the market (`updateRate`), by at most `maxRateStepBps` per update and at most once per `minRateUpdateInterval` seconds - so a keeper key on a server can track the DEX price without being able to move the rate far or fast if it's stolen. Unset: no keeper.

setExternalLimits(uint256,uint256).notice: Sets the external limits (raw USDT units; 0 turns the external path off). What's been paid out against the daily allowance carries over: raising the cap adds the difference to what's available now, lowering it takes it away.

setNativeLimits(uint256,uint256).notice: Sets the native limits (raw USDT units; 0 turns `buy` / `settlePurchase` off), carrying over what's been used today the same way `setExternalLimits` does.

setRateKeeper(address,uint256,uint256).notice: Appoints the keeper allowed to call `updateRate`, and its bounds (`address(0)` removes it).

settleExternalPurchase(address,uint256,s.notice: Settles a purchase paid on a *different* chain - `sourceChain` is a free-form label ("assethub", "ethereum") for logs/events, and `depositId` should be something the relayer derives uniquely from that chain's deposit (e.g. `keccak256(abi.encode(sourceChain, txHash))`) so ids from different sources can never collide. Unlike `settlePurchase`, there is no local USDT balance to check this against - see the contract-level docs on the trust this implies. Bounded by the external limits: over `maxExternalPerDeposit` reverts `OverExternalDepositLimit` (the owner has to raise it for that deposit to ever be paid); over what's left of the daily allowance reverts `OverExternalDailyLimit` (it refills over time).

settleExternalSwap(address,uint256,uint2.notice: Like `settleExternalPurchase`, but at the DEX's market price instead of `rate`: swaps `usdtAmount` of this contract's USDT inventory for XON through Xode's pool and pays the buyer everything the swap returned. `minXonOut` (18-decimal units, like `rate`) is the least the buyer accepts; it should come from the buyer's own deposit, not the relayer. If the pool can't give that much, the whole call reverts and nothing is marked settled, so the deposit can be retried or refunded. Same external limits and relayer trust as `settleExternalPurchase`; the two share `externalSettledDeposits`, so a deposit can only ever be paid one way.

settlePurchase(address,uint256,bytes32).notice: Settles a purchase for a buyer who paid by sending USDT directly (`usdt.transfer`) instead of going through `buy`. Callable only by `relayer`, which is expected to call this once per genuine incoming `Transfer` it observes, identified by that transfer's transaction hash. Safe against a malicious/compromised relayer manufacturing payouts: this only ever succeeds while `accountedUsdt + usdtAmount` stays within the contract's *actual* USDT balance, so a bad relayer can at most misattribute a real deposit, never invent one.

transferOwnership(address).notice: Nominates `newOwner`, who becomes owner by calling `acceptOwnership`. `address(0)` cancels.

updateRate(uint256).notice: The keeper moves `rate` toward the market: by at most `maxRateStepBps` of the current rate, and no sooner than `minRateUpdateInterval` after the last change (by anyone).

withdrawUsdt(uint256).notice: Moves USDT to the treasury (e.g. inventory or proceeds). Draws down `accountedUsdt` first so `settlePurchase`'s balance check stays meaningful after a withdrawal instead of being permanently blocked by funds that already left.

withdrawXon(uint256).notice: Moves XON from the reserve to the treasury - the only place it can go.
